steps_pro.title: Identify the property
steps_pro.text: The applicant enters the block (gush) and parcel (helka). Permit360 loads the registered parcel boundary from the Survey of Israel cadastre.

steps_pro.title: Discover the committee
steps_pro.text: The parcel is intersected with official planning-area boundaries. If it crosses two areas, both candidates are shown with their share of the parcel and the applicant chooses.

steps_pro.title: Understand the building rights
steps_pro.text: Plans covering the parcel are retrieved from XPLAN, with land-use designations and restrictions. Building rights are computed where the rights table is available; otherwise Permit360 lists what is missing.

steps_pro.title: Ask the AI engineering assistant
steps_pro.text: The applicant asks about permitted height or setbacks. The answer is drawn only from the project’s planning package and the committee’s published documents, with every source listed.

steps_pro.title: Prepare the application
steps_pro.text: The wizard collects request type, purpose, documents in PDF, DWG, DXF or XLSX, and the applicant declaration. Each step is saved and can be resumed.

steps_pro.title: Validate before submission
steps_pro.text: The committee’s rule engine runs on the draft and returns a readiness score, blockers and how to fix them. On submission the applicant receives a confirmation number such as P360-2026-000123.

steps_authority.title: Receive the application
steps_authority.text: The request arrives as a case in the committee’s workspace with its documents and confirmation number. Files are classified by content and repeated imports do not create duplicates.

steps_authority.title: Identify applicable regulations
steps_authority.text: The applicable plans, regulations and committee guidelines are assembled for the parcel. Only rules that have been professionally approved and are valid for the case are applied.

steps_authority.title: Analyze the drawings
steps_authority.text: Layers, areas, building lines and setbacks are read from the DWG or DXF geometry. Drawings are compared with the area tables for consistency.

steps_authority.title: Verify measurements
steps_authority.text: Measurements and calculations are deterministic and never performed by the AI model. Measurement uncertainty is carried into the result.

steps_authority.title: Evidence-backed findings
steps_authority.text: Each finding is marked complies, does not comply, requires review or not applicable, and cites the plan clause, regulation or guideline with its page. Findings are marked on the drawing.

steps_authority.title: Track corrections
steps_authority.text: The reviewer accepts or overrides each finding with a reason and returns the case for completions. Every action is written to a tamper-evident audit log.

items.title: Evidence first
items.text: Every finding cites a plan clause, regulation or committee guideline with its page. If the source is missing, the system says so instead of inventing an answer.

items.title: People decide

items.title: Local AI

items.title: Israeli data
items.text: Built on the Survey of Israel cadastre, Planning Administration boundaries, XPLAN plans and committees’ own published documents. The interface is available in Hebrew, English, Arabic and Russian.

faq.q: Does Permit360 issue building permits?
faq.a: No. In Israel the statutory decision on a building permit belongs to the local or regional planning and building committee. Permit360 helps applicants prepare a complete application and helps committees review it, with evidence for every finding.

faq.q: Can I submit my application to Rishuy Zamin through Permit360?
faq.a: Not yet. A live interface to Rishuy Zamin, the national online permit system, is planned. Today, when the committee works in Permit360 the request opens directly as a case in its workspace; otherwise you are told the committee is not connected and must also file in Rishuy Zamin.

faq.q: How does Permit360 know which committee is responsible for my parcel?
faq.a: It intersects the registered parcel boundary from the Survey of Israel cadastre with the official planning-area boundaries published by the Planning Administration. All 131 local and regional committees in the national register are linked by their planning-area codes, and the committee is never guessed from a locality name or plan number.

faq.q: Does the AI decide whether a plan complies?
faq.a: No. Compliance checks and measurements are deterministic and each rule takes effect only after professional approval. The AI is used for classification, extraction and drafting, and the reviewer decides on every finding.

faq.q: Are our documents sent to cloud AI services?
faq.a: No. Language models run on local hardware operated for the platform, and an AI policy per data type blocks any processing location that is not allowed. Using a cloud provider would require the authority’s written approval, and none is approved by default.

faq.q: Who can sign up for Permit360 Pro?
faq.a: Engineers, architects, practical engineers and property owners can register. They verify their e-mail address and the account opens after approval.

building-permit-preparation.title: Building Permit Preparation Software for Israel
building-permit-preparation.description: Prepare a building permit application in Israel from block and parcel: committee, applicable plans, building rights, documents and a pre-submission check.
building-permit-preparation.h1: Building permit preparation software for Israel
building-permit-preparation.lead: Permit360 Pro guides engineers, architects and applicants from a block and parcel number to a complete building permit application. It identifies the responsible committee from official boundaries, gathers the planning information for the plot and runs the committee’s own rules on your draft before you submit.

paragraphs: In Israel, building permits are governed by the Planning and Building Law, 5725-1965, and the Planning and Building Regulations (Building Licensing), 5776-2016. An application is examined by the local or regional planning and building committee against the plans that apply to the plot and against the committee’s own guidelines.

Most delays come from issues that could have been seen in advance: the wrong committee, a plan that covers only part of the parcel, missing documents or area tables that do not match the drawings. Permit360 Pro is built to expose those issues while the application is still yours to fix.

sections.h2: From parcel to application in one workflow
paragraphs: Land in Israel is identified by block and parcel, known in Hebrew as gush and helka. Permit360 Pro starts there, reads the registered parcel boundary and moves through each stage of the request in a guided wizard. Every step is saved, so the work can be resumed at any time.
bullets: Property: block and parcel from the Survey of Israel cadastre
Committee: resolved from official planning-area boundaries
Request type and purpose
Planning information: applicable plans, land uses, restrictions and building rights
Documents in PDF, DWG, DXF and XLSX
Summary, applicant declaration and submission with a confirmation number

paragraphs: The pre-submission check runs the same rule engine that committees use in Permit360 Authority. It returns a readiness score, lists the blockers and explains how to fix each one, and it can compare design alternatives side by side.
Drafts are private to their author. Nothing reaches the committee until you submit.

Each submission receives a confirmation number in the format P360-year-six digits, which is also sent by e-mail. When the committee works in Permit360, the request opens directly as a case in its workspace together with its documents.

When the committee is not yet connected, Permit360 tells you so, and you must also file in Rishuy Zamin, the national online permit system. A live interface to Rishuy Zamin is planned; today Permit360 works with files.

faq.q: Does Permit360 replace the engineer or architect who signs the plans?
faq.a: No. Under the Engineers and Architects Law, 5718-1958, plans are signed by a licensed professional, and that responsibility stays with them. Permit360 supports their preparation work and does not make professional determinations.

faq.q: Can property owners use Permit360 Pro?
faq.a: Yes. Property owners and permit applicants can register alongside engineers, architects and practical engineers. Accounts open after e-mail verification and approval.

faq.q: Which file formats can I upload?
faq.a: The request wizard accepts PDF, DWG, DXF and XLSX documents. Scanned documents without a text layer are not yet read automatically; OCR is planned.

building-permit-review.title: Automated Plan Review for Building Permits in Israel
building-permit-review.description: Automated plan review for Israeli planning committees: document intake, deterministic rule checks with cited sources, CAD analysis and reviewer control.
building-permit-review.h1: Automated plan review with evidence behind every finding
building-permit-review.lead: Permit360 Authority checks building permit applications against approved plan provisions, regulations and committee guidelines. Each finding cites its source with a page reference, and the reviewer accepts or overrides it with a reason.

paragraphs: Applications arrive as PDF, DWG/DXF, DWFX, Excel and ZIP packages. Permit360 classifies each document by its content and extracts the data together with its source, file and page, and a confidence level.

Committee protocols are split into individual requests, and repeated imports of the same material do not create duplicates. Requests submitted from Permit360 Pro arrive as cases with their documents and confirmation number.

sections.h2: A rule engine that shows its work
paragraphs: Checks are deterministic. Measurements and calculations are never performed by the AI model, and every outcome is one of four: complies, does not comply, requires review or not applicable.
Every finding cites the plan clause, regulation or committee guideline it relies on, with its page. Reviewers see why the system reached a result, not just the result.
bullets: A rule takes effect only after professional approval
Rules are versioned and carry validity dates
Checks are re-run when a new version of the application arrives
Findings from drawings are marked on the drawing itself

paragraphs: Permit360 recommends; it does not decide. Reviewers accept or override each finding and record a reason, and the statutory decision remains with the planning committee.
Corrections become classified feedback with regression checks, and accepting a correction requires a second person, a four-eyes control. Accuracy is measured against the reviewers’ own decisions.
Cases, tasks and deadlines are managed in one workspace. Reviewers can return a case for completions, mark it as waiting for external parties and issue a PDF defects report to the applicant.
Every action is written to a tamper-evident audit log built as a hash chain, so the history of a case can be reconstructed and verified.

faq.q: Can a rule change on its own when a regulation changes?
faq.a: No. A source monitor detects changes in regulatory sources and proposes rule drafts, but a rule takes effect only after professional approval. Rules are versioned with validity dates.

faq.q: Does Permit360 connect to our existing permit system?
faq.a: Not yet. Live interfaces to Rishuy Zamin, municipal GIS, permit systems and archives are planned. Today Permit360 works with files and packages.

faq.q: What happens if the system is unsure?
faq.a: The outcome is marked requires review, and measurement uncertainty from the drawings is carried into the result. The reviewer then makes the call.

planning-committees.description: Permit360 Authority for local and regional planning committees in Israel: intake, evidence-based review, reviewer control, workflow and an audit trail.
planning-committees.h1: Permit360 Authority for planning and building committees
planning-committees.lead: Permit360 Authority is the review workspace for local and regional planning and building committees. It turns incoming applications into structured cases, checks them against approved rules with cited evidence and leaves every decision to the committee’s reviewers.

paragraphs: Under the Planning and Building Law, 5725-1965, building permits in Israel are issued by local planning and building committees. Some committees serve a single municipality; others, known as regional committees, cover several localities or the area of a regional council.
Each committee works within an official planning area. Permit360 links all 131 local and regional committees in the national register to their planning-area boundaries by planning-area code.
Permit360 Authority covers the review path from intake to a documented recommendation, with each workspace separated from other authorities.
bullets: Document intake: PDF, DWG/DXF, DWFX, Excel and ZIP, classified by content
Data extraction with source, page and confidence
Deterministic rule checks citing plan clause, regulation or guideline
CAD analysis of areas, setbacks and building lines
Cases, tasks, deadlines, returns for completions and PDF defects reports
Tamper-evident audit log

paragraphs: Rules reflect the plans, regulations and the committee’s own guidelines. A rule takes effect only after professional approval, and rules are versioned with validity dates so a case is checked against the rules that applied to it.

The knowledge base holds committee documents fetched from committee websites and documents uploaded by the platform administrator, searched with keyword and local embedding search. A source monitor detects changes in regulatory sources and proposes rule drafts, never changing a rule automatically.

Every finding can be accepted or overridden with a reason. Corrections become classified feedback with regression checks, and accepting a correction requires a second person. Accuracy is measured against reviewers’ decisions, and the statutory decision remains with the committee.

faq.q: How do applications from Permit360 Pro reach the committee?
faq.a: When a committee works in Permit360, requests submitted from Permit360 Pro arrive as cases in its workspace with their documents and confirmation number. Applicants to committees that are not connected are told to also file in Rishuy Zamin.

faq.q: Is integration with Rishuy Zamin or municipal GIS available?

faq.q: Who can access a committee’s cases?

building-rights.title: Building Rights in Israel: Plans, TABA and Limits
building-rights.description: How building rights are set in Israel by statutory plans (TABA), and how Permit360 computes them for a parcel when the rights table is available.
building-rights.h1: Building rights in Israel, from the plan to the plot
building-rights.lead: In Israel, what you may build on a plot is set by the statutory plans that apply to it, not by the parcel alone. Permit360 finds those plans for the registered parcel and computes building rights when the rights table or plan provisions are available; when they are not, it tells you what is missing.

paragraphs: Building rights are defined in statutory plans prepared under the Planning and Building Law, 5725-1965. The plan that most applicants meet is the TABA, short for Tochnit Binyan Ir, a statutory zoning plan that sets land uses and, typically, quantities such as permitted building area, number of floors and units, height and setbacks.
A parcel may be covered by several plans, some covering all of it and some only part. Reading rights correctly means knowing which plans apply, where, and in what status.

Starting from the block and parcel, Permit360 queries XPLAN, the Planning Administration’s plan system, for plans on the registered parcel boundary. For each plan it shows whether it covers the whole parcel or part of it, its status and its publication.
bullets: Applicable plans and their coverage of the parcel
Land-use designations
Restrictions such as section 77–78 notices and deposited plans
Building rights computed where provisions are available
A clear list of what is still missing

paragraphs: When the rights table or plan provisions are not available in the data, Permit360 does not estimate. It reports what is missing so the professional can obtain it from the plan documents or the committee.
The AI engineering assistant follows the same discipline: numbers that do not appear in the project’s sources are rejected, and every answer lists the sources it used.

Plans in preparation can limit what may be approved today. Under sections 77 and 78 of the Planning and Building Law, notice of a plan’s preparation may be published together with conditions on permits in the area. Permit360 surfaces such notices and deposited plans alongside the plans in force, so they are not discovered late.

faq.q: Is the building-rights result a legal opinion?
faq.a: No. It is a calculation from the available plan provisions, intended to support the professional preparing the application. The binding interpretation rests with the planning committee.

faq.q: Where can I read the plans myself?
faq.a: Plan documents are published on Mavat, the national plan information site. Permit360 shows which plans apply to the parcel so you know what to look up.

committee-lookup.description: Find the planning committee for an Israeli parcel by block and parcel (gush and helka), from official cadastre data and planning-area boundaries.
committee-lookup.h1: Find the planning committee by block and parcel
committee-lookup.lead: Every building permit application in Israel is filed with a specific local or regional planning committee. Permit360 identifies it from the block and parcel by intersecting the registered parcel boundary with the official planning-area boundaries, and never by guessing from a locality name.

paragraphs: Land in Israel is registered by block and parcel, in Hebrew gush and helka. The Survey of Israel cadastre holds the registered boundaries of about 1.1 million parcels, and this is the reference Permit360 uses.
Addresses and locality names are not reliable guides to the responsible committee, particularly near municipal edges and in areas served by regional committees.

Permit360 intersects the registered parcel boundary with the planning-area boundaries published by the Planning Administration. All 131 local and regional committees in the national register are linked to those areas by planning-area code.
bullets: One planning area: the responsible committee is shown
Several planning areas: each candidate committee is shown with its share of the parcel; you choose, and the project is marked not verified
No official answer, for example a parcel not in the cadastre: you may choose manually, and the project is marked unresolved

paragraphs: You can choose the committee from the national committee directory instead. Permit360 then checks that the parcel is inside that committee’s planning area and reports a mismatch if it is not.
Either way, the status of the answer is recorded with the project, so everyone working on it knows how the committee was determined.
The lookup on this website runs on the same official data. To continue with applicable plans, building rights, documents and a pre-submission check, open a project in Permit360 Pro.

faq.q: Why not use the locality name?
faq.a: Because the committee’s jurisdiction is defined by its planning area, not by the name on an address. Permit360 never infers the committee from a locality name or a plan number.

faq.q: What if my parcel crosses two planning areas?
faq.a: You will see both candidate committees with each one’s share of the parcel. You choose, and the project is marked not verified so the choice can be confirmed with the committee.

faq.q: Does the lookup file anything with the committee?
faq.a: No. It only identifies the committee from official boundaries; filing happens through the request wizard or, for committees not connected to Permit360, in Rishuy Zamin.

planning-regulations.title: Israeli Planning Regulations for Building Permits
planning-regulations.description: A guide to Israeli planning regulations for building permits: the Planning and Building Law, licensing regulations, statutory plans and committee rules.
planning-regulations.h1: Israeli planning regulations, explained for permit applicants
planning-regulations.lead: A building permit in Israel is examined against several layers of rules: the Planning and Building Law, its licensing regulations, the statutory plans that apply to the plot and the committee’s own guidelines. Permit360 organizes these layers so that every check can be traced to its source.

paragraphs: The Planning and Building Law, 5725-1965, establishes the planning institutions, the hierarchy of plans and the requirement for a permit. The Planning and Building Regulations (Building Licensing), 5776-2016, set out the licensing procedure and what an application must contain.
The Engineers and Architects Law, 5718-1958, governs the licensing of the professionals who sign the plans. This page is a general orientation, not legal advice.

Statutory plans, including the TABA or statutory zoning plan, define land uses and building rights for specific areas. Committees also publish their own guidelines and procedures, which shape how applications are prepared and reviewed in their jurisdiction.
Plans in preparation matter as well: notices under sections 77 and 78 of the law and deposited plans can affect what may be approved.

sections.h2: How Permit360 turns regulations into checks
paragraphs: In Permit360 Authority, regulations, plan provisions and committee guidelines are expressed as deterministic rules. Each finding cites the plan clause, regulation or guideline it relies on, with its page.
bullets: Rules take effect only after professional approval
Rules are versioned with validity dates

Outcomes: complies, does not comply, requires review, not applicable

paragraphs: The knowledge base holds national knowledge such as laws, regulations and procedures, alongside committee documents fetched from committee websites or uploaded by the platform administrator. A source monitor detects changes in regulatory sources and proposes rule drafts for professional review; it never changes a rule automatically.

faq.q: Does Permit360 provide legal advice?
faq.a: No. It applies professionally approved rules and shows their sources. Interpretation of the law and the statutory decision remain with professionals and the planning committee.

faq.q: Are the official procedures available in English?

cad-gis.lead: Permit360 reads geometry directly from DWG and DXF drawings and checks it against the parcel and the plan. Spatial data from the Survey of Israel cadastre and the Planning Administration’s planning areas anchors every project to its real location.

paragraphs: Permit360 extracts layers, areas, setbacks to plot boundaries and building lines from DXF and DWG files. Measurement uncertainty is carried into the result, so a borderline value is flagged rather than presented as certain.
Findings are marked on the drawing, letting reviewers and designers see exactly where an issue lies.
bullets: Layers and areas
Setbacks to plot boundaries
Building lines
Consistency between drawings and area tables

paragraphs: Measurements and calculations are performed by deterministic code, never by the AI model. The AI is used for classification, extraction and drafting, while compliance outcomes come from approved rules applied to measured geometry.
Each finding cites the plan clause, regulation or guideline it is checked against, with its page.

Parcels come from the Survey of Israel cadastre, covering about 1.1 million registered parcels. Planning-area boundaries come from the Planning Administration, and applicable plans from XPLAN. Spatial data is held in PostgreSQL with PostGIS.
This is what allows Permit360 to identify the responsible committee and the plans covering a parcel from geometry rather than from names.

Today Permit360 works with files and packages: PDF, DWG/DXF, DWFX, Excel and ZIP. Live interfaces to municipal GIS, permit systems, archives and Rishuy Zamin are planned, as is OCR for scanned documents without a text layer.
Until those interfaces exist, applicants and committees upload drawings and documents directly, and the system records the source file and page of every extracted value.

faq.a: Not yet. A live interface to municipal GIS is planned; today the system uses official national datasets and uploaded files.

An AI policy per data type blocks any processing location that is not allowed for that data. Using a cloud provider would require the authority’s written approval, and none is approved by default.

sections.h2: A narrow, defined role for AI
paragraphs: AI is used to classify documents, extract data and draft text. Compliance outcomes come from deterministic, professionally approved rules, and measurements come from deterministic code.

The AI engineering assistant answers only from the project’s planning package and the committee’s published documents, lists its sources and rejects numbers not found in them. Its answers are not a professional determination.

Each authority’s workspace is separated from the others. Permissions are role-based: committees have administrator and reviewer roles, and Permit360 Pro has end users whose drafts are private to their author.
bullets: HttpOnly session cookies
Password policy with scrypt hashing
E-mail verification and approval for self sign-up
Complete audit log

paragraphs: In Permit360 Authority, case actions are recorded in a tamper-evident audit log built as a hash chain. Reviewer decisions, overrides and their reasons are kept with the case, and accepting a correction to the system requires a second person.
Together, local processing, role separation and a verifiable log give committees a clear answer to who changed a case, what the system recommended and who decided.

faq.q: Are documents used to train external AI models?
faq.a: Case documents are not sent to cloud AI services. The language models run on local hardware operated for the platform.

faq.q: Can we allow a cloud AI provider?
faq.a: Only with the authority’s written approval, enforced by the AI policy for each data type. No cloud provider is approved by default.

llms_summary: Permit360 by Kortex Digital Ltd is software for preparing, checking and reviewing building permit applications in Israel. Permit360 Pro serves engineers, architects, practical engineers and property owners: it identifies the responsible planning committee by block and parcel (gush and helka) from the Survey of Israel cadastre and Planning Administration boundaries, retrieves applicable plans from XPLAN, computes building rights when plan provisions are available, and runs a pre-submission check. Permit360 Authority serves local and regional planning committees with document intake, deterministic rule checks that cite plan clauses, regulations and guidelines, CAD analysis, reviewer-controlled findings and a tamper-evident audit log. Language models run on local hardware and never decide compliance or perform measurements; the statutory decision remains with the committee. Integration with Rishuy Zamin, municipal GIS and OCR for scanned documents are planned. The interface is available in Hebrew, English, Arabic and Russian.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement — Permit360
accessibility.description: The Permit360 website accessibility statement: accessibility features, the tests performed and how to contact us about accessibility.
accessibility.lead: We want everyone, including people with disabilities, to be able to use the Permit360 website independently and on equal terms.

paragraphs: The website is built to the WCAG 2.1 level AA guidelines, on which Israeli Standard IS 5568 is based, with the intention of meeting the Equal Rights for Persons with Disabilities (Service Accessibility Adjustments) Regulations, 2013.

bullets: A “skip to content” link at the top of every page
Full keyboard navigation with a clear focus outline
Headings and labelled landmarks for screen readers
Labels on every form field and announced status messages
Checked colour contrast for text and controls
The operating system's “reduce motion” setting is respected — no animation
Right-to-left and left-to-right layouts in four languages

paragraphs: On 27.11.2026, 16 pages (the home page in all four languages and guide pages) were tested with axe-core against the WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 A and AA rules, at desktop and phone widths — no violations were found. Lighthouse accessibility score on the tested pages: 100.
This statement covers the public website. The example screens in the interactive demo are illustrations. The Permit360 application itself, after sign-in, is not covered by this statement.
If something on the website is hard to use or not accessible, please tell us and we will fix it. Write to info@kortexd.com with the page, the problem and the browser or assistive technology you used.
This statement was last updated on 28.11.2026.

privacy.title: Privacy policy — Permit360
privacy.description: What the Permit360 website collects, what it is used for and what happens to it: the demo-request form, the committee lookup and server logs.
privacy.lead: This policy explains what information the public Permit360 website, operated by Kortex Digital Ltd, collects and what is done with it.

paragraphs: The form asks for your name, e-mail, organisation, role, phone and a message — name and e-mail are required, the rest is optional. Sending it requires your consent. The details are e-mailed to the Permit360 team at Kortex Digital only so we can reply, and are not stored in the website's database.

sections.h2: Committee lookup by block and parcel
paragraphs: The block and parcel numbers are sent to our server to find the committee from official data. No personal details are needed, and the result is not stored in any profile.
Like most websites, the server records requests (IP address, time and the address requested) for security and operations. The IP address is also used to limit request rates and prevent abuse.

The public website uses no cookies, no analytics and no third-party tracking, and loads nothing from other websites. After you sign in to the Permit360 application, a sign-in cookie that the application needs is used.
Write to info@kortexd.com to see, correct or ask us to delete the information you gave us, under the Israeli Protection of Privacy Law, 5741-1981.
This policy was last updated on 28.11.2026.
